Laterally_Compressed_Swimming_Tail.description: A long, muscular tail that is laterally flattened like a paddle, featuring a continuous dorsal and ventral fin fold. It acts as the primary means of aquatic propulsion, generating massive thrust through undulating waves.

Prehensile_Arboreal_Tail.description: A slender, grasping tail entirely devoid of swimming fins. Evolved strictly for arboreal salamanders, it curls tightly around branches, functioning as a highly dexterous fifth limb while hunting in the tree canopy.
